title: In need of some feedback : can you run my project well on your PC ?
author: VortexAlthea
selftext:
Hello fellow devs !  
I'm starting to put my game project out there : first upload ever on Itch !  
(The project makes extensively use of AI tools for Sounds and Graphics. But art direction is all mine)   
  
Since my laptop is currently undervolted and under power limits because of overheating issues, I'm right now in a dire need of some technical feedback.   
  
Could you please lend me a few minutes of your time, download and test the game, and tell me how it went ? I'm mainly trying to know how bad the optimization is at this stage.

  
Thanks in advance !



P.S : Do not expect a proper game just yet. It's just the empty environment, beginning and end, but no real content to speak of.

comments.author: Natural-Rich6
comments.body:
Hi If you solo build it so just wow.
A honest review on the graphics and design I prefer more details on the cat, the design is style basic so I guess it will change ( like the green floor)
The fighting is very basic and the all story didn't really understand it.

Good luck 🤞

replies.author: VortexAlthea
replies.body:
Hi there ! Thank you so much for taking the time to play and write a feedback, I appreciate it !

May I ask how well it ran on your machine ? Did you encounter a lot of stutters and lag ? Or was it smooth all the time ? Do you have an high end PC ?

Yup ! It’s only me and my AI workflow (Dream by Wombo for designs and textures, ChatGPT for some clean up and then Tripo to turn characters and objects to 3D, then animate in Mixamo or by hand in Blender sometimes.). I also use bought assets for buildings and animals (like the cat, hence why you maybe felt it was generic). And of course ElevenLabs for sound design.

I’ll see what I can do to adress the points you raised as development progresses :)

(Story is actually supposed to be very straightfoward but set within a weird dreamy setting. And actually the green floor is solid water haha. I’ll add particle effects and maybe a displacement map later in development to make it more visible. Regarding combat yeah, I was hesitant on cutting it completely since it’s not the focus of the game… but ultimately it will serve only as a « last chance » in case of failstate during stealth, once I get it working.)

replies.author: Natural-Rich6
replies.body:
I run it on vm ( windows with 16 ram 2 core) so to give you how it run will not be right but is was playable.
I will try to send to friends I know how review is important.
I make video games but I am not really a gamer...

replies.author: VortexAlthea
replies.body:
That’s very kind of you man, thanks a lot !!!
Glad to hear it was at least playable ! I don’t know much about virtual machines or cloud gaming, but I’m assuming it uses a quite capable cpu and graphics card… I’ll guess I won’t know more until more people play and give feedback.

Thanks again for your input and for offering to share with your friends. As you said, reviews are invaluable, especially in this early stage. It’s hard for me to focus on the creative part if I’m constantly worried about lags and stutters ^^
